title: Construction of a high-nuclearity Nd(III) nanoring for the NIR luminescent detection of antibiotics

synthesis.procedure: At room temperature, Nd(OAc)3·6H2O (0.20 mmol, 0.0643 g) and H2L (2,3-dihydroxybenzaldehyde; 0.40 mmol, 0.0609 g) were dissolved in 10 mL MeOH, then 1.0 mol L−1 triethylamine in 1 mL EtOH was added. The mixture was heated under reflux with stirring for 30 min, cooled to room temperature and filtered. Slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the clear solution for one week produced red crystalline 1. The lanthanide-complex synthesis was carried out using Schlenk techniques.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature dissolution, then reflux for 30 min, then cool to room temperature
synthesis.time: 30 min reflux; diethyl ether diffusion for one week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk techniques; reflux then diethyl ether vapor diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: cooled and filtered; slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the clear solution for one week gave red crystals

properties.summary: Upon ligand-centered excitation at 404 nm in CH3CN, 1 shows typical Nd(III) NIR emission at 881, 1064 and 1340 nm via ligand-to-metal energy transfer. NIR lifetime 7.94 μs; intrinsic Nd quantum yield 3.18%; overall quantum yield 0.16%; sensitization efficiency 5.03%. The nanoring acts as a NIR luminescent sensor for antibiotics, with high selectivity/sensitivity to nitrofuran antibiotics (NFAs) attributed to an inner-filter effect; KSV = 1.05×10^4–2.33×10^4 M−1 and LOD = 3.05–6.75 μM, and the NFA response is retained in mixtures and in real antibiotic drugs.
